recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is for FHIR-14114. No core follow-up is needed for the phase element itself; any further review of phase terminology or binding strength should be handled under the later terminology trackers rather than this STU3 element-addition issue.
issue_request: FHIR-14114 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 change request asking that phase be specifically named on ResearchStudy instead of being folded into category/classifier semantics; Jira records that the change was made and published in the Dec 2017 FHIR ballot.
initial_application: No current git commit message explicitly names FHIR-14114 or GF#14114, but commit 61b5fa557635a9d272e7508b2c7e139a895be930 added ResearchStudy.phase as a 0..1 CodeableConcept in the ResearchStudy spreadsheet on 2017-11-13 and removed Study Phase from the broader classification list. Commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 preserved the element during the 2021 source refactor into structuredefinition-ResearchStudy.xml.
additional_context: FHIR-14115 is the duplicate retracted/no-change tracker for the same request. FHIR-14161 added the associated value set, FHIR-14288 adjusted the original binding decision, and later R6 work including FHIR-50710 moved ResearchStudy.phase terminology to THO. These related terminology decisions affect binding details but do not reverse the seed issue's explicit phase-element requirement.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. ResearchStudy is active in source/fhir.ini, and source/researchstudy/structuredefinition-ResearchStudy.xml currently defines ResearchStudy.phase as a distinct 0..1 CodeableConcept with clinical-trial phase semantics, a THO phase value set binding, and mappings. The current classifier element also warns not to use generic classifier semantics for meanings already represented by explicit elements.
